visual_style: Vertical 9:16, warm natural daylight, gentle realistic cinematic look. A Pakistani government school: whitewashed walls, a green blackboard, wooden desks, pupils in school uniform. Modest dress. No on-screen text, captions, logos or watermarks in the frame.

narrator.name: the narrator
narrator.description: A Pakistani woman teacher in her thirties in a plain shalwar kameez with a dupatta, warm and confident, speaking directly to the camera.

shots.visual: Inside a crowded Class 5 room of about fifty pupils, some leaning forward eagerly, some distracted; the narrator stands at the front, turns to the camera and speaks.
The narrator at the blackboard with a simple chalk sketch of a child growing from toddler to teenager; she turns to the camera as she speaks.
Pupils working in small groups at their desks; the narrator kneels beside a quiet pupil and encourages her, then looks up at the camera.
The narrator walks between the rows checking exercise books, nods at a pupil's work, then speaks to the camera from the middle of the room.
The narrator in the school corridor holding a phone showing a textbook page, smiling and speaking to the camera; pupils pass softly in the background.

narration: Same class, same lesson. Why do some pupils learn fast while others fall behind?
Educational Psychology shows how children grow, think and learn, from development to memory and problem-solving.
You will study motivation, intelligence, individual differences and special needs, and how to manage a real classroom.
Twelve units, from assessment to well-being and guidance, with Pakistani classroom examples throughout.
Study the full course free at textbook dot com dot pk. The link is below.
